_comment: Migration Validator — Multi-Source Enhanced Rules Catalog v4.0. Optimized for MSServer, PostgreSQL, and Athena → Snowflake migrations. Includes all normalization rules with source-specific variants.

rules.description: Normalizes boolean values to text '1' (true) or '0' (false) for consistent comparison across all source databases. Eliminates case differences (true vs TRUE vs True).
rules.pg_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = true THEN '1' WHEN {col} = false THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.mssql_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = 1 THEN '1' WHEN {col} = 0 THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.athena_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = true THEN '1' WHEN {col} = false THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.sf_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = TRUE THEN '1' WHEN {col} = FALSE THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.notes: MS SQL Server BIT type (0/1) normalized same as boolean. Athena uses Presto boolean semantics.

rules.description: Casts numeric/decimal values to text at full native precision — no rounding. Surfaces real precision drift instead of hiding it.
rules.notes: 2dp rounding removed by team decision. MS SQL Server MONEY/SMALLMONEY still compared as decimal text, at full precision, no rounding.

rules.description: Formats timezone-naive timestamps to microsecond precision. Fractional seconds are compared, not stripped.
rules.notes: Second-precision truncation removed by team decision. MS SQL DATETIME (only ~3.33ms native precision) and SMALLDATETIME (minute precision) will show trailing zeros/rounding vs DATETIME2 — that's expected, not a bug.

rules.description: Converts timezone-aware timestamps to UTC then formats to microsecond precision. Eliminates timezone offset differences while still comparing fractional seconds.
rules.athena_expression: DATE_FORMAT(CAST({col} AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%S.%f')
rules.notes: MS SQL Server DATETIMEOFFSET includes timezone offset — converted to UTC, then compared to microsecond precision.

rules.description: Formats DATE columns as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text for uniform comparison across all sources.
rules.notes: DATE type is consistent across all sources — only formatting differs.

rules.description: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from string columns. Empty string '' remains distinct from NULL. This is also the DEFAULT FALLBACK for unrecognized type pairs.
rules.notes: MS SQL Server requires LTRIM(RTRIM()) — TRIM() not available until SQL Server 2017. NVARCHAR/NCHAR (Unicode) treated same as VARCHAR/CHAR.

rules.description: Converts UUID/GUID to text and trims spaces. Case is NOT normalized — a real case difference between source and target now surfaces as a mismatch.
rules.notes: UPPER() removed by team decision. MS SQL Server UNIQUEIDENTIFIER is the GUID type. PostgreSQL stores UUID in lowercase — if Fivetran uppercases it in Snowflake, that will now show as a mismatch by design.

rules.description: Casts integer-family columns to text for cross-system comparison. Eliminates type-width mismatches (INT32 vs INT64 vs NUMBER).
rules.notes: MS SQL Server has TINYINT (8-bit) not in PostgreSQL. Athena uses standard SQL integer types.

rules.description: Converts JSON into canonical text representation before comparison. Eliminates key-ordering and formatting differences.
rules.notes: MS SQL Server stores JSON as NVARCHAR(MAX) — no native JSON type until SQL Server 2016. JSONB in PostgreSQL auto-sorts keys.

rules.description: Converts binary data into hexadecimal text representation. Enables text-based comparison of binary columns.
rules.notes: MS SQL Server IMAGE type is deprecated but still common in legacy schemas. CONVERT style 2 = hex without 0x prefix. MSSQL TIMESTAMP/ROWVERSION types are binary and should be EXCLUDED (not compared).

rules.display_name: HStore → CAST to TEXT then TRIM
rules.description: Casts PostgreSQL hstore (key-value store) to TEXT before trimming. Fivetran converts hstore to JSON-like text in Snowflake.
rules.notes: PostgreSQL-specific type. Not available in MS SQL Server or Athena.

rules.description: Converts XML columns to trimmed text. MS SQL Server XML type and PostgreSQL XML type both normalized.
rules.notes: MS SQL Server XML type is complex — casting to NVARCHAR(MAX) may truncate very large XML.

notes: SERIAL/BIGSERIAL are integer types with auto-increment
JSONB stores JSON in decomposed binary format (faster, sorted keys)
Arrays, ranges, and composite types require special handling (not yet supported)
HStore is PostgreSQL-specific key-value type
System columns (xmin, xmax, ctid) should be excluded
TIMESTAMP/ROWVERSION is a BINARY auto-increment counter, NOT a datetime — must be EXCLUDED
NVARCHAR/NCHAR are Unicode types (UTF-16) — treated same as VARCHAR/CHAR in validation
UNIQUEIDENTIFIER is the GUID/UUID type
MONEY/SMALLMONEY have fixed 4 decimal places — rounded to 2dp for validation
XML type requires CAST to NVARCHAR(MAX) — may truncate very large XML
IMAGE/TEXT/NTEXT types are deprecated — use VARBINARY(MAX)/NVARCHAR(MAX) instead
BIT type is boolean (0/1) — normalized to '0'/'1' text
LTRIM(RTRIM()) required for trimming — TRIM() only available since SQL Server 2017
Athena is query engine over S3 data — schema defined in Glue catalog
Uses Presto/Trino SQL dialect
Virtual columns like $path, $file_size should be excluded
DATE_FORMAT function uses MySQL-style format strings (%Y-%m-%d)
No native UUID type — use STRING/VARCHAR
Arrays and structs supported but require special handling
Decimal precision may differ from source — always normalize to 2dp

null_rule.description: Universal NULL handling applied to ALL columns. SQL NULL ≠ NULL (NULL comparisons return NULL/unknown). Converting NULL to '<<NULL>>' sentinel makes equality comparisons work correctly. Applied as the outermost COALESCE wrapper after all other transformations.
null_rule.notes: Applied to EVERY column regardless of source database or data type.

fivetran_filter.description: Snowflake-side filter added when _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE column is detected. Ensures only the LATEST active record is compared instead of historical Fivetran change-tracking snapshots.
fivetran_filter.notes: Auto-detected by SnowflakeExtractor.has_fivetran_active(). Only applied to Snowflake queries.

rule_application_order.description: Rules applied innermost to outermost — type-specific transformation first, NULL placeholder last.
order: integer (CAST to text — innermost for integer types)

recommendations: Always test validation rules against sample data from each source database
Use exclusions.yaml to exclude problematic columns (e.g., MS SQL TIMESTAMP/ROWVERSION)
For large tables (>10M rows), consider sampling or partitioned validation
Monitor validation query performance — indexes on join columns are critical
MS SQL Server: Check for Unicode vs non-Unicode type mismatches (NVARCHAR vs VARCHAR)
PostgreSQL: Check for array/composite types — may need custom handling
Athena: Partition filtering is critical for performance on large S3 datasets
Always normalize timestamps to UTC and strip microseconds
Round all numeric types to agreed precision (default 2dp)
Test NULL handling — source databases may have different NULL semantics
